summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for an episode of hematemesis followed by dizziness and syncope. Evaluation confirmed no active variceal bleeding, and the bleeding was attributed to gastric antral vascular ectasia (GAVE), with stable hemoglobin throughout. Abdominal pain in the right upper quadrant was consistent with prior findings of intestinal malrotation. He was managed with intravenous pantoprazole, transitioned to high-dose oral pantoprazole, and started on sucralfate for gastric protection. His cirrhosis remained stable without signs of decompensation. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue medications, avoid alcohol, follow up with his liver specialist, and consider iron supplementation once symptoms resolve.
problems: Angiodysplasia of stomach and duodenum with hemorrhage
